Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Horsell, Surrey, 1894, firelight and black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:03. The shot opens on a medium close shot on a woman jammed in the road between the banks at night, a woman of thirty in a dark shawl over a pale blouse with her hair coming down, her head turned back over her shoulder toward the red glow behind, her mouth wide open, packed black coats pressing against her on both sides. The camera is down in the road among them, level with her face, two paces from her, a 50mm lens, a low angle. The red glow behind her is the only light. At the first frame the woman's head and shoulders fill the CENTRE of the frame, the panel cutting her at the middle of the chest. The shot is inside this place: the narrow stretch of the Chobham road at night in 1894, where it runs down between high sandy banks: the road pinched to a cart's width, raw sandy banks rising steeply on both sides above head height with heather and gorse roots along their tops, cart ruts worn deep down the middle of it, the way ahead black. The camera keeps low in the road, a static shot at the height of her face with the packed coats all round as she looks back over her shoulder at the red sky and shouts, from 00:00 to 00:02. <Subject 1> (S1), on screen, a person, with a clipped English voice at an even pace, says: <d>[English] They're coming!</d> His mouth shapes every syllable as the line is heard and closes on the last word. At 00:02, as the line ends, her free hand comes up against the coat of the person in front of her and pushes, and the push continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:03 the camera is keeping through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
